claims.claim: Asterius of Amasea was Bishop of Amasea in Pontus, made bishop between 380 and 390 AD after having been a lawyer.
Asterius of Amasea was born in Cappadocia around 350 AD and died around 410 AD.
Asterius was educated by a Scythian slave who had acquired an excellent education at Antioch.
Sixteen homilies and panegyrics on the martyrs survive, showing familiarity with the classics and containing details of everyday life.
One sermon, Oration 4: Adversus Kalendarum Festum, attacks the pagan customs and abuses of the New Year's feast, denying everything that Libanius had said supporting it.
This sermon against the Calends was preached on January 1, 400 AD, which provides main evidence for dating his career.
Oration 11, On the martyrdom of St. Euphemia, describes a painting of the martyrdom and compares it to pictures by Euphranor and Timomachus.
The text of Oration 11 was quoted twice by the Second Council of Nicaea in 787 as evidence in favour of the veneration of images.
